subject: Crash with the second use of readMP3

messages.author: 16d37ab18c8885a4
messages.subject: Crash with the second use of readMP3
parts:
On Windows, with R 3.1.1, I have a crash with this program:
  library(tuneR)
  library(seewave)
  mp3 <- "198096"
  f_mp3 <- sprintf("%s/%s.mp3", mp3Dir, mp3)
  chant <- mono(readMP3(f_mp3), "left")
  print(chant)
  mp3 <- "101545"
  f_mp3 <- sprintf("%s/%s.mp3", mp3Dir, mp3)
  chant <- mono(readMP3(f_mp3), "left")
  print(chant)

The mp3 come from xeno-canto.

Any idea ?

  library(tuneR)
  library(seewave)
  Drive <- substr( getwd(),1,2)
  mp3Dir <- sprintf("%s/XENO", Drive)

    dir.create(mp3Dir)

}
  mp3 <- "198096"

if ( ! file.exists(f_mp3) ) {
    url_mp3 <- sprintf("http://www.xeno-canto.org/%s/download", mp3)
    download.file(url_mp3, f_mp3, quiet = FALSE, mode = "wb",)

}
  chant <- mono(readMP3(f_mp3), "left")
  print(chant)
  mp3 <- "101545"
  f_mp3 <- sprintf("%s/%s.mp3", mp3Dir, mp3)

if ( ! file.exists(f_mp3) ) {
    url_mp3 <- sprintf("http://www.xeno-canto.org/%s/download", mp3)
    download.file(url_mp3, f_mp3, quiet = FALSE, mode = "wb",)

}
  chant <- mono(readMP3(f_mp3), "left")
  print(chant)

Hello,
It seems that there is a bug with readMP3() as a simple 1 s pure tone
sound saved in mp3 cannot be read (see below).
I will contact the maintainer of tuneR to ask advice and come back to
the list if I get informaiton
Best
Jerome
